claims.statement: Nonreciprocal current can arise in time-reversal symmetric Bloch electrons when finite dissipation enables interband processes.
claims.downstream: Motivates the Green-function formula and the geometric conductivity (C2).
blockers: Conceptual claim. The S-matrix unitarity argument is local algebra under S†S=I; the physical leap from non-unitarity to interband DC current is not a compiled residual.

claims.statement: In TR-symmetric systems the longitudinal conductivity is geometric: \(\sigma^{\alpha\alpha\alpha}\) is built from the shift vector \(R_{ab}\) and Berry connections, Eq. (5), starting from the Green-function kernel Eq. (4).
appendix_chain: Appendix C: static σ from ∂ω²K and band-basis I^(1,2,3)
claims.downstream: C3–C5 all quote Eq. (5). If C2 fails, the scaling and numerics lose their analytic parent.
blockers: The Appendix D algebra (antisymmetrization, shift-vector identity, H=ξ i A substitution) is not compiled as local A−B=0.
TR matrix-element identities are representation-theoretic, not a checked residual.

claims.statement: For an insulator/semiconductor (\(\mu\) in the gap) at low \(T\) (\(\Gamma\ll\xi_{\min}\), \(\beta\Gamma\gg 2\pi\)), \(D^{(2,3)}=O(\Gamma^2)+O(\Gamma^3)\), so \(\sigma^{\alpha\alpha\alpha}=O(\Gamma^2)\).
assumptions: \(\mu\) inside the gap so \(\xi_{\min}\le|\xi_a|\) for all bands
claims.downstream: Rice–Mele semiconducting \(\Gamma^2\) curves (C5) are consistency checks of this scaling.
blockers: Finite displayed terms do not prove the O(Γ³) remainder.

claims.statement: At high \(T\) (\(\beta\Gamma\ll 2\pi\)), or when \(\mu\) lies in a band, the leading piece is \(O(\Gamma)\).
claims.locator: Results, Eqs. (10)–(11) and the metallic paragraph
appendix_chain: same D kernels; no extra appendix identity
assumptions: or metallic: some \(\xi_a=0\), so the low-T \(\xi_{\min}\) argument is unavailable
blockers: O(Γ²) remainder in Eqs. (10)–(11) is declared, not certified.
Metallic O(Γ) is a domain argument, not a compiled expansion.

claims.statement: A 1D Rice–Mele calculation produces \(\sigma^{xxx}(\mu,\Gamma,T)\) consistent with dissipation-induced geometric current in a TR-symmetric inversion-broken insulator/metal, and an order estimate for 3D polar semiconductors.
appendix_chain: Appendix E order estimation (unnumbered Hamiltonian in main text)
assumptions: parameters \(m=\delta t=0.1 t_0\) in the figures
TR preserved so Drude and QMD vanish in this model
claims.downstream: Does not prove Eq. (5). Supports observability claims in the Discussion.
blockers: Numerical evaluation of a model is consistency, not derivation.

reviewer_obligations.claim_used: Gauge invariance removes the \(O(\omega^0)\) and \(O(\omega)\) pieces of \(\mathcal{K}(\omega,-\omega)\), so static \(\sigma\) is the \(\omega^2\) term.
reviewer_obligations.why_not_certified: This is a physical gauge/Bloch argument, not a local symbolic identity A−B=0. Appendix A also invokes that a static vector potential is unphysical.
reviewer_obligations.paper_evidence: Main text after Eq. (3); Appendix A, undifferentiated K and \(\partial_{\omega_1}^2\mathcal{K}|_{0,0}\) vanishing.
reviewer_obligations.reviewer_must_decide: Confirm that, under the declared Bloch + velocity-gauge assumptions, the two leading orders in ω vanish identically so that Eq. (3) is the DC conductivity.

reviewer_obligations.claim_used: TR symmetry T=KU(k→−k) implies the two H-matrix identities used to antisymmetrize the longitudinal kernel.
reviewer_obligations.why_not_certified: Requires the antiunitary representation of TR on Bloch states. Not encoded as a compiled residual.
reviewer_obligations.paper_evidence: Appendix D, two numbered lines after Eq. (D-1).
reviewer_obligations.reviewer_must_decide: Accept \(\langle a|\partial_\alpha H|b\rangle=-\langle b|\partial_\alpha H|a\rangle|_{k\to-k}\) and the corresponding \(\partial^2 H\) identity under the paper's T.

reviewer_obligations.claim_used: After TR, Green-function monomials may be replaced by antisymmetrized equivalents (\(\overset{\mathcal{A}}{=}\)).
reviewer_obligations.why_not_certified: Local algebra of the 𝒜 steps was not compiled.
reviewer_obligations.paper_evidence: Appendix D, four 𝒜 replacements on G^R, G^A strings.
reviewer_obligations.reviewer_must_decide: Either accept the 𝒜 calculus as written, or request a compiled identity for each replacement.

reviewer_obligations.claim_used: The TR rewrite of \(\sum H_{ba}^{\alpha\alpha}H_{ab}^\alpha F(a,b)\) produces the shift vector \(R_{ba}\) and the triple-A term, which become Eq. (5) after \(H=\xi i A\).
reviewer_obligations.why_not_certified: Named geometric identity plus substitution; not a machine residual.
reviewer_obligations.paper_evidence: Appendix D, F(a,b) display through the last sentence of the appendix.
reviewer_obligations.reviewer_must_decide: Confirm the shift-vector identification and the final substitution that yields Eq. (5) from Σ^{ααα}.

reviewer_obligations.claim_used: Finite Γ is the physically relevant non-unitarity that realises C1.
reviewer_obligations.paper_evidence: Introduction, imaginary part of the self-energy; constant Γ in G^{R,A}.
reviewer_obligations.reviewer_must_decide: Accept constant-Γ relaxation as the dissipation model of the paper.

reviewer_obligations.claim_used: \(\psi(z)\sim\log z\) plus the stated \(\Gamma,\beta,\xi\) regime justify C3/C4.
reviewer_obligations.why_not_certified: Asymptotic remainder. Finite displayed polynomials are not an O(·) proof.
reviewer_obligations.reviewer_must_decide: Accept the digamma expansion and domain split (gap vs band, low-T vs high-T) without a remainder certificate.

reviewer_obligations.claim_used: Rice–Mele numerics confirm dissipation-induced σ^{xxx} in a TR-symmetric model.
reviewer_obligations.why_not_certified: Numerical support, not analytic certification of Eq. (5).
reviewer_obligations.paper_evidence: Model calculation; Figs. colorMapvsMu and riceMelevsGamma; Appendix E.
reviewer_obligations.reviewer_must_decide: Treat the figures as consistency in one 1D model (and an order-of-magnitude 3D estimate), not as a proof of the geometric formula.

reviewer_obligations.why_not_certified: Standing assumption; poles merge if bands coincide (Appendix C).
reviewer_obligations.paper_evidence: Results after Eq. (5); Appendix C ‘we assume that there are no degeneracies’.
reviewer_obligations.reviewer_must_decide: Accept the nondegeneracy hypothesis for the geometric formula and the clean-limit cases.

numerical_evidence.supports: C3/C4 scaling and C2’s claim that TR-symmetric inversion-broken crystals can carry this current
numerical_evidence.proves_not: Does not prove Eq. (5), the Appendix D identities, or remainder bounds.
